rounds.text: Astron Multigrain Ltd presents a significant disconnect between its reported accounting profits and its actual ability to generate cash, as evidenced by a negative cash conversion ratio of -2.14x [E26]. The company’s operating cash flow has plummeted to Rs -7.39 Cr, resulting in a free cash flow deficit of Rs -10.96 Cr as of March 2026 [E27, E28]. This liquidity strain is compounded by deteriorating operational efficiency, with debtor days ballooning from 86.8 to 127 days and working capital days increasing from 65.4 to 112 days [E41, E42]. Furthermore, the company’s profitability is trending in the wrong direction, with compounded profit growth for the trailing twelve months sitting at -10% and operating margins contracting by 4 percentage points over the last three years [E19, E23]. While the company reports profits, the absence of any dividend payout suggests these earnings are not being effectively converted into shareholder returns [E4, E40]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.14x and has demonstrated strong historical sales growth [E14, E29].
